Methods for joint scale fits

Source: R/joint_scales_methods.R
multiScaleR_joint-methods.Rd

Print, summarize, and extract results from a joint fit made with multiScale_joint(). logLik() makes stats::AIC() and stats::BIC() work, so several structures fitted to the same data sets can be compared directly. anova() gives likelihood-ratio tests between nested structures. A test of a "common" fit against a "footprint_scaled" fit tests kappa = 0, on the boundary of the parameter space, and uses the matching mixture of chi-square distributions (half the chi-square p-value for one kappa).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_joint'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_joint'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_multiScaleR_joint'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_joint'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_joint'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_joint'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_joint'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR_joint'
anova(object, ...)

Arguments

x, object

A multiScaleR_joint object.

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Further multiScaleR_joint objects for anova(); ignored by the other methods.

Value

print() returns x invisibly. summary() returns an object of class summary_multiScaleR_joint holding the parameter, scale, comparison, and per-data-set coefficient tables. logLik() returns a logLik object whose df counts every native parameter plus the joint scale parameters, kappa, and shared coefficients. coef() returns the joint parameters on their natural scales (scales in map units). vcov() returns their covariance on the optimizer scale (log scales, kappa, coefficients). nobs() returns the total number of observations. anova() returns a data frame of likelihood-ratio tests.

See also

multiScale_joint()
